question: Add Krag Peak as a peak area plus the SE Ridge route from Crater Lake? How does our Krag Peak Traverse relate?
answer: Krag Peak is a double-topped peak: 9,092 ft lidar (Peakbagger, most recent; Oregon Hikers 9,048 ft), coordinate 45.06523,-117.28951 (PB; OH 45.06523,-117.28915). Crater Lake is the base camp (East Eagle Equestrian Trailhead 45.04774,-117.32771; 13.6 mi RT, 3,490 ft to the lake). The standard line from the lake is a ridge with several humps ending in a loose class 3 headwall, about 2.5 h round trip from the lake (fetched 2003 report, in snow). Naming disagrees: Oregon Hikers says northeast ridge via the east ridge; a summit-page snippet says southeast ridge, class 3 (not fetched). Our Krag Peak Traverse is a different, harder loop: East Eagle trail 1.5 mi, steep loose west rib to the west summit, across to the higher east summit, then down to Crater Lake and Little Kettle Creek trail (FKT page: 10.76 mi, 4,888 ft, both summits). It descends by the standard ridge, so it is distinct but overlaps.
recommendation: ADD new peak area 'Krag Peak' under parent or_wallowa_mountains at 45.06523,-117.28951, elev 9092 ft; ADD route 'Southeast Ridge from Crater Lake' (scrambling, class 3, Aug-Sep); move 'Krag Peak Traverse' onto the new area and keep it (rename optional 'West Rib Traverse'). Run catalog_find_area('Krag Peak','Oregon') first. Season Aug-Sep per ascent histogram (21 of 26 logged in Aug-Sep).

routeRow.name: Southeast Ridge from Crater Lake
routeRow.overview: The short standard way up this double-topped summit, started from the Crater Lake basin. Easy talus leads to the ridge, which has several humps and fades near the top, ending in a loose headwall scramble. Snow on the scree in autumn makes it much worse.
routeRow.approach: From East Eagle Equestrian Trailhead take the Little Kettle Creek trail up more than 25 switchbacks to Crater Lake (3,490 ft of gain). Leave the lake basin and climb toward the ridge.
routeRow.descent_text: Descend the ridge the way you came, staying below the crest where it is easier.
